uncited: It solves the problem of efficiently generating volumetric representations for real-time applications by mapping screen-space coverage to voxel-space occupancy.
**Primitive Generation**: Each occupied voxel is represented by one or more geometric primitives.
**Coordinate Transformation**: Voxel indices $(i, j, k)$ are transformed into world space.
**Rasterization**: The generated primitives are transformed into clip space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix and rasterized.
**Culling**: To manage performance, frustum culling is applied to exclude voxels outside the camera view.
- **Pitfall**: Edge expansion causes extra pixels to be shaded (yellow pixels in Figure 9), particularly for thin triangles, leading to unnecessary pixel shader calls.
- **Definition**: Using hardware-supported conservative rasterization available on Maxwell base chipsets or higher via NVAPI.
The method originated from the need to efficiently voxelize triangle meshes for real-time global illumination and ray tracing on GPUs.
Early implementations relied on standard rasterization, which suffered from gaps ("holes") when primitives fell between pixel centers or when projection directions changed.
The technique is widely used in real-time rendering engines for voxel cone tracing, voxel-based lighting, and volumetric data visualization.
